overview: Enjoy one of the first cultural and tourism cruises of its kind in Abu Dhabi. Experience an unique form of edutainment (Education and Entertainment) created to enrich people's knowledge on the history of the pearling industry in the Arabian Gulf region, and how many of the countries forefathers dedicated their lives to collecting thousands of seashells in hope to find a pearl.
highlights: Travel by boat and see the sights from the water
expect: Enjoy a unique experience in Abu Dhabi that’s both educational and entertaining, and learn about the traditional pearl industry of the Arabian Gulf. Your cruise will start following a pick-up from any hotel in the city, climb aboard a traditional jalboot (a pearl fishing dhow), and depart from the Eastern Mangroves Hotel and Spa. Set off on a leisurely cruise along the quiet channel between Abu Dhabi and the Hudairi Yat islands. Seated on traditional Arabian floor cushions, enjoy locally made Arabic coffee and dates, while an Emirati guide explains how the country’s forefathers dedicated their lives to finding valuable pearls to trade or make jewelry. Watch how to open a living oyster, before being invited to search for a pearl yourself. After the seashells have been opened with an oyster knife, look for your own pearl to keep as a souvenir. Local Arabic snacks will be served as you sail, while a crew member sings some authentic Emirati seafaring songs.

overview: Discover one of the gems of the UAE on this Dubai sightseeing day trip from Abu Dhabi. Travel by air-conditioned coach as your guide sheds light on the region’s rich history and culture. Admire top local attractions such as the Palm Jumeirah, Burj Al-Arab and the breathtaking Burj Khalifah. Cruise across Dubai Creek on a wooden ‘abra’ taxi and shop till you drop in the bustling gold and spice souks. highlights: Dubai day trip from Abu Dhabi by air-conditioned coach
Behold the spectacular Burj Khalifah, the world’s highest building
See top Dubai attractions including the Palm Jumeirah and Burj Al-Arab
Visit Dubai Museum and sail Dubai Creek on a wooden abra

expect: Meet your guide at your central Abu Dhabi hotel, then hop aboard a comfortable, air- conditioned coach. Gaze out at the desert and Arabian Gulf as you travel to Dubai and, after around 1.5 hours on the road, relish your first sight of its skyscrapers, rising mirage-like from the desert.

Drive to the Palm Jumeirah, the man-made archipelago shaped like a palm tree and marvel at the mighty Atlantis, The Palm hotel that soars up from its outer edges. Admire the sail-shaped Burj Al-Arab hotel, one of the world’s tallest hotels at 1,053 feet (321 meters), and crane your neck to see the tip of the breathtaking Burj Khalifa, the world’s tallest building at 2,716 feet (828 meters) as your guide explains how it took six years to build with up to 12,000 workers on site each day.

Stop at Dubai Mall, the city's state-of-the-art shopping mall, and enjoy free time for some retail therapy or lunch (own expense) at any of the restaurants or food courts. Pay a visit to Dubai Museum, housed in the 18th-century Al Fahidi Fort, and trace the city’s rise to 21st-century metropolis through the interesting displays, replica buildings and other exhibits.

Sail across Dubai Creek on a traditional abra water taxi and delve into the Deira district to visit its souks. Stroll around the Gold Souk past shops shining with gold and precious stones; and explore the traditional Spice Souk, where the stalls brim with exotic spices, herbs and other goodies. Get haggling tips from your guide and perhaps snap up some bargains as reminders of your day.
When your Dubai tour ends, return to Abu Dhabi where your day finishes with a hotel drop- off.

title.en: Al Ain Day Trip from Abu Dhabi with Lunch

overview: Discover the picturesque city of Al Ain on a day trip from Abu Dhabi. Travel through the desert to the ‘Garden City,’ framed by the rugged Hajar Mountains. Chart the city’s history at Al Ain National Museum; visit the Sheikh Zayed Palace Museum; and witness the water channels that irrigate the palm groves. Gain insight into traditional life at the markets and camel race circuit; and admire city views from nearby Jebel Hafeet mountain. Dip your feet into Al Ain’s springs and seal your trip with an included buffet lunch.
highlights: Day trip to Al Ain from Abu Dhabi with a local guide
Explore the UAE’s oasis “Garden City,” known for its green parks
Visit Al Ain National Museum and Sheikh Zayed Palace Museum
See the traditional falaj water channels amid the oasis palms
Travel up Jebel Hafeet mountain for epic city views
Walk around a food market, camel racetrack and mountain springs
Savor a buffet lunch of international cuisine at a 4-star hotel
expect: Leave your central Abu Dhabi in the morning by air-conditioned coach, and travel through the desert toward Al Ain, located near the UAE-Oman border.

Often dubbed the ‘Garden City,’ this picturesque town is one of the UAE’s oldest and lies at the foot of the craggy Hajar Mountains. During your journey, hear about Al Ain’s past, and how the discovery of ancient tools and burial mounds nearby has revealed that people settled here as far back as in Bronze Age times.

Pass the lush gardens and tree-lined avenues on the outskirts as you head for Al Ain National Museum. Go inside and enjoy a tour of the historical exhibits and some of the Bronze Age relics displayed nearby.
Drive to the intriguing Sheikh Zayed Palace Museum, home of the UAE’s late founder, His Highness Sheikh Zayed. Step inside to ogle the beautiful interiors, art gallery, meeting rooms and gardens.

Then, visit three top Al Ain attractions — the camel racing circuit and the livestock market and food market — for a peek into the daily rituals and dealings of its citizens. See the ‘falaj’ channels dug to transport water around the date palms, and hear how this simple system has been used to irrigate crops for thousands of years. Drive the winding roads up the high slopes of Jebel Hafeet, the 4,098-foot (1,249-meter) mountain that towers over Al Ain. Stop here to drink in the bird’s-eye views over the city and the surrounding peaks.

Then, head back down to the hot springs in the foothills. Soak up the gorgeous scenery and perhaps cool your toes in the springs. Then, relax over lunch at a local hotel. Dig into buffet dishes such as grilled meat and fish, and enjoy drinks at your own expense. Your experience finishes with a drop-off back at your Abu Dhabi hotel.

expect: Begin your half-day tour with a pickup from your central Abu Dhabi hotel. As you travel, hear fascinating facts about the Liwa Oasis, a series of oases at the north of the Rub Al Khali or "Empty Quarter," the world’s largest desert of continuous sand. This immense desert extends from the southern UAE to southern Saudi Arabia, and into Oman and Yemen, and was once home to the tribes who went on to settle Abu Dhabi. Along the way, gaze out at the desert scenery and watch as the sand changes color from creamy yellow to dark orange. Then, after around two hours, arrive on the outer fringes of Liwa and marvel at the ocean of dunes that stretches endlessly before you. Follow the black-topped roads through the dunes and feel the thrill as your driver steers you off road onto the sands for a roughly 2-hour desert drive. Have your camera ready as you rumble past the incredible dunes, lush oases, desert settlements and camel farms. As you explore, your guide will point out places of interest and interesting indigenous flora. Keep a watch, too, for desert wildlife such as the nimble Arabian gazelle, rabbits and lizards, and hear how they forage for food and water in this arid expanse. After working up an appetite, stop at an oasis to enjoy a delicious picnic lunch. Savor goodies such as chicken pasta, fruit salad and muffins teamed with refreshing soda and water, and drink in the overwhelming silence and sense of emptiness around you as you eat. Explore further after lunch and then, when the time comes, head back to the bustle of Abu Dhabi. Your trip ends with a drop-off back at your hotel in the late afternoon.

expect: Paintball is a game that incorporates skills where-in two teams compete in games of capture, elimination or stealth. Though the games objectives may vary, the way to victory is to mark your opponent with a Paintball Gun while trying to achieve a set task using teamwork and strategy. Teams are usually 3/5/7/10 each side strong and can have up to 2 substitute players. With the opposing team eliminated and/or the task achieved, a horn sounds the end of the game with a winning team.

Your experience starts by dividing all the players in two groups to determine which overall colors are used by each side. You will be then directed to the locker rooms to suit up, next the protective gear is issued like masks, vests or neck bands. Lastly, the "marker" is issued. The field marshals will brief all of you in regards to the markers mechanisms and handling, game mechanics, safety. Safety is observed at all times that's why the markers are only loaded upon entry in the playing field. The field marshals acts as referees in the field and instructors for each game tasks which varies from capture the flag to protecting a co player. Both teams go to each designated home base as a starting point. When everything is set a horn will sound off to start game. Use teamwork and strategy in getting the upper hand to defeat the other team. The game is over upon hearing the final horn and the marshals determine the winner of the game.

expect: When your ship is docked in Mina Zayed cruise port in Abu Dhabi, step ashore and travel independently into the city to the excursion starting point. Board your comfortable, air- conditioned coach and head for the Sheikh Zayed Bin Sultan Al-Nahyan Mosque, Abu Dhabi’s best-known landmark Usually known as the Grand Mosque, this vast place of worship is one of the world’s biggest mosques, and named after the late Sheikh Zayed, considered the founding father of the UAE. Admire the gleaming white domes and minarets, and then go inside to view the opulent interiors with your guide. Extravagantly decorated with marble mosaics, crystal chandeliers and a colossal Persian carpet, the mosque boasts a huge prayer hall and was designed to accommodate around 40,000 worshippers.

Next, enjoy a panoramic coach tour of Abu Dhabi’s other landmarks. Snap photos of the monumental Emirates Palace Hotel and enjoy the views as you trace Abu Dhabi Corniche – the curving palm-lined waterfront — to the Breakwater marina, bobbing with billion-dollar yachts and famous for stellar views of the city’s skyscrapers. Break for lunch (own expense), and, in the afternoon, visit the Abu Dhabi Falcon Hospital, a modern health center for injured and sick falcons, the UAE’s national bird. Falcons are central to the national heritage, and these magnificent birds are revered as symbols of power and courage.

With a highly trained falcon carer, explore the clinical and health facilities, and hear how the hospital has extended its care to other avian species. Learn about the treatments on offer, and afterward, stroll to the outdoor aviary for an impressive flying display. If you wish, have a photo taken with some of the majestic birds before your tour concludes at the original starting point.

Then, hop inside your air-conditioned minivan and set off to see the highlights of the city. Capital of the United Arab Emirates, Abu Dhabi is often called the Arabian Jewel – a name that testifies to the city’s lavish monuments and flashy modern architecture.

As you travel around town, listen to your guide’s stories about the city and, of course, its fascinating sights. Luckily, your first stop is at one of Abu Dhabi’s undisputed best: Sheikh Zayed Bin Sultan Al-Nahyan Mosque, or the grand mosque, as it is more simply known. Head inside to learn about the monument and marvel at its sheer size and grandeur. The stunning building can accommodate some 40,000 worshipers inside its walls, making it one of the world’s largest mosques.

Hop back inside your minivan and travel the short distance to Zayed Centre, a museum dedicated to the late Sheikh Zayed – a leader affectionately known by his people as the ‘father of the nation.’ Step inside and browse an impressive collection of Zayed memorabilia, seeing photos, his cherished cars and, even, gifts of stuffed lions and cheetahs. After learning about the man who is said to have shaped the United Arab Emirates, travel to your final stop of the tour: Abu Dhabi Heritage Village. The open-air museum showcases life in the city before the discovery of oil, so look out for recreated souqs (markets) as well a traditional Bedouin camp complete with goat-hair tents.
Finish your tour with a drive along the stunning Corniche with its famous white-sand beach, and then say your goodbyes to your guide back at the start point. Worry-free Shore Excursion:

overview: Explore top attractions in the UAE’s capital on this 4-hour Abu Dhabi sightseeing tour. Travel through Abu Dhabi by air-conditioned coach as a guide sheds light on the region’s rich culture and heritage. Marvel at the soaring domes and minarets of Sheikh Zayed Mosque. Mingle with the locals in the bustling souks, where everything from gold jewelry to fresh dates has a price to barter on. Then, travel past the corniche’s pristine gardens and beaches to the Heritage Village, where the Abu Dhabi of old is brought to life.
highlights: 4-hour sightseeing tour of Abu Dhabi
Explore Abu Dhabi by air-conditioned coach with a guide
Gain insight into the city’s transformation from fishing village to buzzing metropolis
Take in famous landmarks including the Sheikh Zayed Mosque

expect: Begin your 4-hour tour with a pickup from your central Abu Dhabi hotel. Hop inside your air- conditioned coach to travel around the UAE’s beautiful capital, often dubbed the ‘Arabian Jewel’ for its gleaming landmarks and stunning architecture. Along the way, hear fascinating facts about the city’s past and present, and the plans for its future. Learn how the discovery of oil in 1958 saw it transform from a fishing port into today’s metropolis in just a few decades.

Head to the Sheikh Zayed Mosque, known as the Grand Mosque, and one of the world’s biggest mosques. Admire the spectacular domes and minarets of this vast white marble edifice, and go inside with your guide to view the interior as you learn how the mosque can accommodate some 40,000 people.

Travel to the Souk and work your way around this bustling marketplace. Stroll past the outlets stacked with gold jewelry and perhaps snap up some of the wares as you explore Next, visit the Dates Market, where shops sell enormous quantities of fresh dates and other sweet treats. Admire the pyramids of the fresh, juicy palm fruits, and sample some of the tasty treasures as your guide explains why they hold a special place in Abu Dhabi’s heritage. Pass futuristic buildings and the gardens and beaches of the beautiful corniche on route to the Heritage Village, an open-air museum that recreates a typical Emirati desert village of old. Peep inside the goat-hair Bedouin tents and reconstructed huts to discover what life was like here before oil. See craftspeople making pottery, watch a traditional falaj irrigation system in action, shop for souvenirs at the souk, and visit the museum to chart Abu Dhabi’s history through photographs and other exhibits.
After around four hours of exploring the city, your tour finishes with a hotel drop-off.

expect: Start your experience with a pickup from your central Abu Dhabi hotel. Then, relax in your air-conditioned coach and set off on your sightseeing as your guide explains how, until the 1950s, Abu Dhabi was little more than a small fishing port.

Hear how Abu Dhabi’s fortunes changed in 1958 with the discovery of oil, and how this ushered in massive investment, seeing it mushroom into today’s futuristic emirate, and carving out its state-of-the-art architecture including space-age towers and and extravagant leisure developments.

Head out of town to Masdar City, one of the emirate’s grandest-ever building projects. This incredible — and as yet unfinished — renewable-energy city is ingeniously designed to stay cooler than the surrounding desert.

See some of Masdar, and then travel to Yas Island, the artificial island just outside Abu Dhabi. Stroll around Yas and admire the extravagant Yas Viceroy Hotel on the Yas Marina F1 circuit before heading for Ferrari World, the world’s first Ferrari theme park. While your visit doesn’t allow time for rides, it offers a fascinating insight into Abu Dhabi’s latest attractions. Shop for Ferrari souvenirs if you wish, and enjoy free time for lunch (own expense).

Next, visit man-made Saadiyat Island, home to art centers and museums. Pose for photos at the dune-shaped UAE Pavilion and visit the Manarat Al Saadiyat to see scale models and a video showcasing Abu Dhabi’s future development.

Finally, return to the city and see its best-known landmark, the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque. Admire this white-marble mosque and hear how it accommodates 40,000 worshippers, making it one of the world’s largest.
After snapping photos here, end your tour with a drop-off at your Abu Dhabi hotel.
